body: claimed: qsmits (Claude Code, Opus 5.5) · 2026-11-27T08:02Z · worktree/branch none · plan: research

Research note 1: the maintainer's first answer (Discord, before a detailed read of this issue).

> "if u wanna do UI/UX correctly, that work needs to be collected into a Crate"

What we changed:

- The body has a new section "Plan, step 0: the UI kit crate". The crate `crates/ui-kit` holds the tokens, the theme and the components. It depends on `egui` only, not on `camcraft-app`.
- PR K makes the crate before the other UI pull requests. PR A depends on K.
- Question 7 asks for the scope: a crate for the design system, or crates for all UI code.

Open questions: 1 to 7 in the body.

Research note 2: what can move into `crates/ui-kit` now.

We read the UI code on `main` (no build). Paths are under `crates/ui/src/egui_app/`.

| Group | Files | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| Move as they are (egui and std only) | `theme/` (clamp, dropdown, legal, live, tables), `contrast.rs`, `theme_files/names.rs`, `window_chrome.rs`, `layout/controls.rs`, `layout/field_ring.rs`, `layout/scroll_gutter.rs`, `layout/form.rs` (status banner and action bar) | about 1490 |
| Move with a small seam | `theme.rs`, `theme_files.rs`, `theme_files/overlay.rs`, `ribbon_cell.rs`, `icons.rs` | about 1270 |
| Stay in `crates/ui` | `theme_drop.rs`, `layout/setups.rs`, `layout/mod.rs` (dock and app state) | about 700 |

The seams:

1. `theme_files.rs` uses `camcraft_app::schema::ThemeRef`. The kit gets its own small enum (dark, named theme, theme file). `crates/ui` converts `ThemeRef` to it.
2. `theme.rs` and `theme_files/overlay.rs` use `light_ground` from `ground_ink.rs`. `ground_ink.rs` also uses the colour-vision tables, so only `light_ground` (10 lines) moves.
3. `ribbon_cell.rs` uses the constant `UV_FULL` from `painted.rs`. The constant moves.
4. `icons.rs`: the generic icon set moves. The table of CAM icon slots (Pocket, Drill, Probe and others) stays in `crates/ui`. The `include_bytes` paths change.

Other facts:

- `layout/form.rs` has 420 lines, more than the 400-line rule. PR K splits it: the status banner and the action bar become their own files. Both are pure egui. Their callers in `op_page.rs` and `pages.rs` stay.
- The workspace pins egui, egui-wgpu and eframe at `=0.36.2`. The kit uses the same pins.
- `crates/ui` builds for wasm32. No candidate file has a wasm `cfg`, and their dependencies are wasm-safe. The kit builds for wasm32 too.

Result for PR K: about 2760 lines move, with four small seams. No app logic moves. The PR is a move, with no change of behaviour. It is large in lines but simple in logic. We can split it in two parts: (a) the theme and contrast, (b) the layout widgets, ribbon cell and icons.

Not checked yet: the test files of these modules. They move with their modules, and the `crates/ui` test count must stay the same or grow (#1953).

Maintainer answers to questions 1 to 7. The maintainer gave them in a question dialog on 2026-11-27. An agent of the maintainer session posts them.

1. Direction: **yes**. CamCraft is a CAM tool first. Side panes are docked when open, and they fold to title chips.
2. Minimum screen size: **1366 × 768**.
3. In-app menu bar (PR E): **yes**.
4. Engine items of step 2: **yes, as design issues**. Code can start as soon as the maintainer accepts a design note. No item waits for the path kernel.
5. Cut groups: **yes**. The maintainer still names the cut list at each cut.
6. #661: it **follows this plan**. The icons follow the CAM-first design. The SolidCraft icon style is no longer a goal of #661.
7. UI kit crate: **one crate for the design system only** (tokens, theme and components), as in step 0. The panes stay in `crates/ui`.

You can now file the sub-issues of step 1 and step 2 and link them here.
Generally i think the design language should follow Solidcraft - the screenshots looks a bit much like a react web page..

Research note 3: the answers of the maintainer, and the design language.

The maintainer answered questions 1 to 7 (comment of 2026-11-27 08:09). The plan stays as in the body, with these answers:

- CAM tool first. Docked panes fold to title chips. Minimum screen size 1366 × 768. In-app menu bar: yes.
- The engine items are design issues. Code starts when the maintainer accepts a design note.
- The cut groups stay. The maintainer names each cut list.
- #661 follows this plan. The SolidCraft icon style is no longer a goal of #661.
- The UI kit crate is for the design system only. The panes stay in `crates/ui`.

Design language (maintainer comment of 08:10, confirmed on Discord): the workflow is CAM-first, and the visual language follows the principles of SolidCraft. The mockups E1 and E2 look too much like a web page. Rules for the kit:

- Panes are flat and docked to the window edges. A hairline separates them. No card frames, no gaps around the panes.
- No shadows.
- Small corner radii.
- Structure comes from type: small section headers with a thin rule, values at the right. No boxes inside boxes.
- Compact rows and a small title.
- The status is a slim banner with an accent bar, not a card.
- A folded pane is a docked header strip, not a floating pill.
- Tags (source of a value, state) are plain text with a glyph, not coloured pills.

We build these principles in our own kit, in our own words and code. The SolidCraft kit, its assets and its palettes stay under its licence (#655, `P?`). Our token names are our own, so a SolidCraft palette can map in later if the licence permits it.

Next: new mockups in this style, then the sub-issues of step 1 and step 2.
